text: In February 2018 Toronto Council approved the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority capital budget which included a project known as Menno-Reesor Restoration Project, which supported the restoration of the 27 hectare site for the use of a new Toronto Wildlife Hospital. The project is one of Toronto's largest restoration sites and work on the site includes converting a former corn field into a healthy renaturalized area that will be home to the largest wildlife hospital in Canada and will include numerous cages and pens to house hundreds of wild animals while they recover from injuries. The project includes protecting, restoring and expanding existing natural areas, regrading the site back to a more natural landscape, removing old tile drain, recreating a healthy stream onsite along with a significant amount of riparian habitat, reforestation of parts of the site, meadowland…

City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council include restoration of the heritage barn and home at 6461 Steeles Avenue East, as part of the already approved 2018 Council Toronto and Region Conservation Authority capital budget allocation for the restoration project.
